title: Google Workers Expose Lifetime Gag Clauses After AI Military Protests

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Google employees are bound by contracts that prohibit them from criticizing the company for the rest of their lives, according to testimony given to the BBC. Sofia Liguori, who recently resigned and spoke to the broadcaster, said staff fear retaliation and career risk if they publicly voice concerns about artificial intelligence safety and Google's intelligence contracts for warfare.

Researchers at Google DeepMind are subject to non-disparagement clauses in perpetuity that forbid any critical remarks about the company. While some former staff members have chosen to go public, these restrictions have discouraged others and created a chilling effect on discussions regarding the safety and risks of military AI.

selectedTweets.text:
"""
Employees at Google have told the BBC that staff are scared to speak out about AI safety and its uses in warfare because their employment contracts prohibit them from publicly criticising the company.

"In principle I'm not allowed to criticise Google for the duration of my life," Sofia Liguori told the BBC. But she decided to do so "because I believe it's important for these things to be known and I also think that talking about facts is not criticising".

Liguori added that at Google "people are scared of retaliation and putting their career at risk. You feel you are being watched, you can't speak."
"""

selectedTweets.text:
Important, and I'm glad this is finally public. Google DeepMind researchers are under in perpetuity non-disparagement clauses forbidding them from ever speaking critically of the company. I'd already confirmed this with multiple people.

Yes, some ex-employees have spoken out nonetheless. But it has also discouraged others from doing so. And yes, it most certainly has a chilling effect with regards to discussions on safety and risk.

Others have written compellingly about how important the ability to speak freely and critically is, especially on topics like safety and risk. And what a testament to the research employee community's coordination and hard-won bargaining power it has been to get there at other companies.

GDM burn that commons by having this. And everyone who signs burns that commons too. Let's get it changed.
